recipes.name: Mediterranean Grilled Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 4 bone-in pork rib chops (not pork loin chops) - at least 1/2-inch thick

steps.text: Mix together sage, rosemary, salt, thyme, fennel, sugar, and bay leaf in a bowl until thoroughly combined.
Rub both sides of pork chops with herb mixture and coat them with olive oil. Refrigerate for several hours or overnight.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.

Grill chops until they are browned, show good grill marks, and the meat is no longer pink inside, about 4 minutes per side. An instant-read meat thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a chop should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Mediterranean Grilled Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: These Mediterranean pork chops are simple yet tasty. Use an herb rub with sage, rosemary, and more to infuse these easy grilled chops with flavor.

review.reviewBody: I've noticed that the reviewers who only give this a 4-star rating each left off one ingredient. This is one of the few recipes i would never change - the salt is essential for flavor, and the sugar is essential for both flavor and crisping the edges. Still, reviews aren't bad! Thanks, and also thanks for the pic - i don't have a camera.
The taste was unspeakable. A good mix of herbs is what made this dish fantastic. I then used my Traeger and smoked at 180F for about an hour than adjusted the temperature to 350F for a final cook.

My husband and I both liked this pork and the spice combination. I left out the salt and sugar but it was delicious without them. I marinated them for about 3 hours. Since our grill died, I sauteed the boneless pork loin chops for a couple of minutes on each side to brown and then put them in a baking dish with a little chicken broth and baked them at 350 for about 30 minutes. I would make this again. Thank you Stormy3600 for sharing the recipe.

I used 4 tbsp of brown sugar instead of the white sugar, & added 1/2 tsp instant coffee grinds for a little more twang. We had fresh rosemary instead of dried, & that made a huge difference too. The whole family was wowed & my wife wants me to make this next time we have back yard dinner party.

I used boneless sirloin chops since I didn't have bone in chops. I followed the recipe as is but added several cloves of minced garlic to the herb mixture and a teaspoon of Sage and brushed the chops with balsamic vinegar as I grilled them. Very tasty and tender. My husband gave it a thumbs up!!!

Delicious dry rub for grilled pork chops! I let the spice blend sit on the chops for only 30 minutes and it was still delicious. I left out the fennel, because we aren't fans but added about a 1/2 tsp of garlic powder and squeezed a little lemon juice on the chops once they were done cooking. Perfection!!

Both my husband and I have enjoyed this easy, delicious way to grill pork chops. We made it many times exactly as written, except left out the fennel because my husband doesn't care for it. The flavors blended nicely (even without the fennel). I'm going to try it tonight with pork tenderloin for the first time. Hopefully, it will be just as tasty on the leaner pork. Thanks for the recipe!

My husband and I both LOVED this recipe! I followed the recipe exactly, except I only marinaded for 3 hours due to time constraints. I broiled for 4-5 minutes on each side. I'm thinking about making it in mass quantities and giving it out as Christmas presents in jars.

Very tasty! I did not have time to marinate it for the time specified in the recipe so the rub/olive oil was basically added and then it went into the oven. Still it came out very yummy. My husband even thought it did not have sufficient salt/taste and that I could have increased the salt/spices (opposite of what I said in other reviews were people said it was too salty). I did not have the fennel seed or the dried sage unfortunately, but still it tasted great, as if I ordered from a restaurant!

I paired it with another recipe for Mediterranean Roasted Potatoes which was a great combo. Link to the Potato recipe: http://allrecipes.com/recipe/mediterranean-roast-vegetables/detail.aspx?event8=1&prop24=SR_Title&e11=mediterranean%20potatoe&e8=Quick%20Search&event10=1&e7=Home%20Page

Any time my husband ooohs and aaahs over my dinner, I HAVE to give the recipe a 5! So there you are! We really did enjoy this. I did cut the recipe in half because there were just the two of us. I made the rub exactly as stated in the recipe and put them and the olive oil on my bone-in pork chops about 8 hours before grilling them, and they were really good! Thanks for the recipe, Stormy!

Absolutely amazing! We're not big pork chop fans - but this recipe changed that! I did add lemon juice as other suggested and went a smidge lighter on the rosemary as it can be over powering. Really wonderful and easy recipe!
Juicy! Only way from now on and did on the grill, I know neighborhood had to be envious
Made the recipe with ingredients stated. Short on time, so only marinated for about an hour, but they were still very flavorful. Will definitely make again!
Love the seasoning! Will save this recipe to make again.
We really enjoyed this combination of herbs, and I love that it is not drenched in a sweet, tomato-y sauce. Thanks for a great method for grilling pork chops!

Great rub for pork chops! I only marinated for 30 minutes and left out the fennel. (Don’t really like fennel) Grilled bone in chops to 145 degrees F. Drizzled a little lemon juice over the when done. Perfection!
I used 3/4" thick bono chops and it turned out wonderful. sorry forgot to take a picture but, they were beautiful and delicious.
